messages:
maria: heads up — when I quick-switch between workspaces i sometimes see rows from the previous org in the console table. repro: 1) quick-switch to org-A 2) open saved search 3) quick-switch to org-B 4) open same saved search -> see org-A rows. screenshot attached.
cheng: ugh. do you have network trace or headers? might be a cache key issue. can you paste the offending request?
maria: paste:
```http
GET /api/console/search?q=status%3Aopen&limit=50 HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.internal
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Accept: application/json
# note: missing X-Workspace-ID header
```
ryan: this looks like hydration cache keyed on user+route but not workspace id. console-hydration map uses session id only. i remember a change in https://github.com/redwood/console/commit/abcdef that flattened the key.
lisa: quick mitigation: invalidate hydration cache on quick-switch, or include workspace in the key. patch should be tiny.
sam: telemetry shows correlated spike in cross-org resultsets around 2026-03-18 14:12 UTC: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/console/tenant-leak?panel=3 :arrow_right: +1.3% cross-tenant hits
maria: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4521 — adds X-Workspace-ID to cache key and fallback invalidation + test. will run staging canary.
cheng: run canary in staging and watch rollout dashboard (console.rollout.hydration_leak). add alert for >0 cross-tenant hits. also do quick audit for other caches (prefetch, runlist).
maria: on it. i'll coordinate a canary at 10:10am PST and ping here. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started for pr/4521 -> staging-canary (build 3421)
maria: canary looks clean so far (staging) — no cross-tenant rows after 20 mins smoke. will request prod canary tomorrow.
cheng: +1. keep an eye on latency impact from larger cache key. if perf regresses, consider separate per-workspace caches with LRU size tune.
ryan: long term we should add unit tests that spin quick-switch sequences to catch regressions. i'll add to eng-platform tests.
lisa: created ticket ENG-8764 to audit other caching layers
maria: thanks everyone, closing the loop. :sparkles:
